quote: Theorem 1. Let X1, X2 and Y1, Y2 be 2 pairs of independent random variable such that Xi ∼ W − G(αi, β, γi) and Yi ∼ W − G(αi*, β, γi*) for i = 1, 2. Whenever w(x) is an increasing convex function, also w′′(x) is increasing and β ≥ 2, [[α1, α2],[γ1, γ2]] ∈ P2, then [[α1, α2],[γ1, γ2]] ≺≺ [[α1*, α2*],[γ1*, γ2*]] ⇒ X1:2 ≥hr Y1:2.
family: Weibull-G family W−G(α, β, γ): H(x) = 1 − exp(−α (w(γx))^β), with w(F(x)) = F(x)/(1 − F(x)) for baseline scale-family cdf F(γx)
compared: 2×2 parameter matrices (α; γ) under multivariate chain majorization ≺≺, with row-comonotonicity set P2

hypotheses.text: w(x) is an increasing convex function, also w′′(x) is increasing
hypotheses.formal: w' >= 0, w'' >= 0 increasing (w''' >= 0 used in proof)
chain majorization: [α;γ] = [α*;γ*] T for a T-transform matrix

quote: Example 1. Let X1, X2 be independent random variables such that Xi ∼ W − Exp(αi, β, γi), i = 1, 2. Also let Y1, Y2 be another pair of independent random variable such that Yi ∼ W − Exp(αi*, β, γi*), i = 1, 2 (the baseline distribution is Exponential with cdf, F(x) = 1 − e^{−γx}). The parameters are given in the form of matrices as [[α1*, α2*],[γ1*, γ2*]] = [[4.8, 3.4],[2.5, 1.6]] ∈ P2 and [[α1, α2],[γ1, γ2]] = [[4.03, 4.17],[2.005, 2.095]]. It can be observed that [[α1, α2],[γ1, γ2]] = [[α1*, α2*],[γ1*, γ2*]] T^{0.45}, and it satisfies the condition [[α1, α2],[γ1, γ2]] ≺≺ [[α1*, α2*],[γ1*, γ2*]] ⇒ X1:2 ≥hr Y1:2.
family: Weibull-exponential W−Exp(α, β, γ): baseline F(x) = 1 − e^{−γx}, w(t) = t/(1−t)

conclusion.direction: X1:2 >=hr Y1:2 (Figure 1 plots rY1:2 − rX1:2 >= 0 for β = 3)

quote: Theorem 4. Let X1, X2, . . . , Xn be a set of independent random variables from Weibull-G distributed family of distribution such that Xi ∼ W − G(αi, β, γ) for i = 1, 2, . . . , n. Let Y1, Y2, . . . , Yn be another set of independent random variables such that Yi ∼ W − G(αi*, β, γ) for i = 1, 2, . . . , n. Then α ≺w α* ⇒ Xn:n ≤rh Yn:n.
family: Weibull-G W−G(αi, β, γ); common β and γ
